source: Open Library + Google Books metadata; covers via Open Library Covers; blurbs written for collinslab

books.title: Lincoln in the Bardo
books.author: George Saunders
books.tagline: One night, one grieving father, countless ghosts.
books.blurb: In 1862 the President's young son is laid in a borrowed crypt, and Abraham Lincoln returns alone after dark to hold him. Around them, a chorus of restless dead argue, joke and confess, refusing to admit where they are. Saunders builds a novel out of voices, and it lands as a meditation on grief that is as funny as it is shattering.

books.title: The Underground Railroad
books.author: Colson Whitehead
books.tagline: The railroad is real. So is the chase.
books.blurb: Cora, a young woman enslaved on a Georgia cotton plantation, takes a desperate chance on escape. In Whitehead's reimagining, the Underground Railroad is a literal network of tracks and tunnels, and each state she surfaces in is its own kind of trap. A propulsive, unflinching novel about freedom and the country that keeps withholding it.

books.title: Hamnet
books.author: Maggie O'Farrell
books.tagline: A plague summer, a twin, a playwright's grief.
books.blurb: In Stratford in the 1580s, a fiercely independent woman who knows the secrets of plants marries a Latin tutor with restless ambitions. Years later, while he works in London, sickness reaches their household. O'Farrell imagines the family behind Shakespeare's most haunting title, with the mother at the centre of the story.

books.title: Normal People
books.author: Sally Rooney
books.tagline: Two people who keep finding their way back.
books.blurb: In a small Irish town, popular Connell and solitary Marianne begin something secret that neither can quite explain. Through school, Trinity College and the years after, they drift apart and back again, misreading each other in ways that feel painfully familiar. A precise, intimate novel about class, power and how hard it is to say what you mean.

books.title: Demon Copperhead
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.tagline: Appalachia's orphan, telling it straight.
books.blurb: Born in a trailer to a teenage mother in the mountains of southern Virginia, Demon has wit, talent and almost no luck. Foster care, child labour, football glory and the opioid wave all come at him in turn. Kingsolver reworks David Copperfield for modern Appalachia in a narrator's voice you will not forget.

books.title: The Overstory
books.author: Richard Powers
books.tagline: Nine lives, bound together by trees.
books.blurb: An artist, a soldier, a scientist, a programmer and others each discover, in their own way, that trees are trying to tell them something. Their paths converge in the fight to save the last old forests of the American West. A sweeping novel whose real protagonists have roots.

books.title: Shuggie Bain
books.author: Douglas Stuart
books.tagline: A boy in Glasgow, loving his mother anyway.
books.blurb: In 1980s Glasgow, as the mines and shipyards close, Agnes Bain clings to glamour and dignity while drink pulls her under. Her youngest son, Shuggie, a boy who never fits in, is determined to save her. A tender and devastating debut about poverty, addiction and a love that will not quit.

books.title: Klara and the Sun
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.tagline: An artificial friend, watching and hoping.
books.blurb: From her place in a shop window, Klara, a solar-powered companion, studies the people who pass and waits to be chosen. When she joins the household of a fragile teenager, she brings a devotion that is almost religious. Ishiguro's quiet, luminous novel asks what it means to love someone, and to be human at all.

books.title: Small Things Like These
books.author: Claire Keegan
books.tagline: A coal merchant's Christmas, and a choice.
books.blurb: In a small Irish town in 1985, Bill Furlong delivers coal and timber and keeps his head down, as most people do. A delivery to the local convent shows him something he cannot unsee. A short, perfectly made novel about ordinary decency and what it costs.

books.title: Homegoing
books.author: Yaa Gyasi
books.tagline: Two sisters, two continents, three hundred years.
books.blurb: Half-sisters born in eighteenth-century Ghana never meet: one marries an English officer, the other is sold into the Atlantic slave trade. Each chapter follows a descendant through the generations, in Africa and America, down to the present. A bold debut that makes history feel personal, one life at a time.

books.title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
books.author: Gabrielle Zevin
books.tagline: Two friends, thirty years, a hundred games.
books.blurb: Sam and Sadie meet as children in a hospital games room, lose touch, and reunite at college with the idea for a video game. What follows is a partnership that brings fame, rivalry and wounds neither can name. A novel about creative collaboration and the kind of love that isn't romance.

books.title: Prophet Song
books.author: Paul Lynch
books.tagline: When your own country turns, slowly.
books.blurb: On a dark Dublin evening, two officers of a new secret police come to Eilish Stack's door asking for her husband. As Ireland slides into authoritarian rule, she fights to hold her four children and her family together. A breathless, urgent novel of a crisis that feels unnervingly close.

books.title: Project Hail Mary
books.author: Andy Weir
books.tagline: One astronaut, no memory, a dying sun.
books.blurb: A man wakes aboard a spacecraft light-years from Earth with no idea who he is, and two crewmates long dead. As memory returns, he realises the survival of humanity depends on him and his schoolteacher's grasp of science. A problem-solving adventure with a big heart and an unlikely friendship.

books.title: Piranesi
books.author: Susanna Clarke
books.tagline: Endless halls, tides, statues, and one devoted explorer.
books.blurb: Piranesi lives in the House, an infinite labyrinth of marble halls where the ocean rises through the lower floors. He catalogues its statues and tides and meets only one other person, twice a week, until he finds evidence of someone new. A strange, beautiful puzzle of a novel.

books.title: The Fifth Season
books.author: N. K. Jemisin
books.tagline: The world ends again. She keeps going.
books.blurb: On a supercontinent wracked by seismic catastrophes, people born with the power to move the earth are feared, controlled and used. As a new apocalypse begins, a woman sets out across a broken land after her stolen daughter. The first of a trilogy that won three Hugo Awards in a row.

books.title: Children of Time
books.author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
books.tagline: Humanity's last ark meets a new civilisation.
books.blurb: A terraforming experiment goes wrong, and on a distant green planet something other than monkeys inherits an accelerated evolution. Millennia later, the last humans arrive in a battered ship looking for a home. An epic of first contact told from both sides.

books.title: A Memory Called Empire
books.author: Arkady Martine
books.tagline: A new ambassador. Her predecessor's ghost. Intrigue.
books.blurb: Mahit Dzmare arrives at the heart of the Teixcalaanli Empire to find the previous ambassador from her small mining station dead, and nobody admitting how. With an outdated copy of his memories in her head, she has to navigate poetry, politics and a city that wants to swallow her world.

books.title: Circe
books.author: Madeline Miller
books.tagline: A minor goddess finds her own power.
books.blurb: Born to the sun god but scorned in his halls, Circe discovers she has a talent for witchcraft and is banished to a lonely island. There she crosses paths with gods, monsters and mortals out of Greek legend. A myth retold from the inside, fierce and humane.

books.title: Gideon the Ninth
books.author: Tamsyn Muir
books.tagline: Lesbian necromancers, haunted palace, swordplay.
books.blurb: Gideon wants nothing more than to escape the gloomy Ninth House and its bone-witch heir, Harrowhark. Instead she is drafted as Harrow's cavalier for a deadly trial in a decaying palace by the sea. Gothic, irreverent and full of swagger, it is a locked-room mystery in space.

books.title: The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet
books.author: Becky Chambers
books.tagline: A patched-up ship and its found family.
books.blurb: Rosemary joins the Wayfarer, a tunnelling ship with a crew of humans, aliens and one wise AI, and takes the job of a lifetime: a long haul to a distant, contested world. Along the way the real adventure is getting to know each other. Warm, generous space opera.

books.title: The Wager
books.author: David Grann
books.tagline: Shipwreck, mutiny, and a battle over the truth.
books.blurb: In 1740 a British warship sails to chase Spanish treasure and is wrecked off the coast of Patagonia. Months later, two very different bands of survivors return home with very different stories. Grann reconstructs a true tale of survival, empire and who gets to decide what really happened.

books.title: Erebus
books.author: Michael Palin
books.tagline: One ship, two poles, a famous disappearance.
books.blurb: HMS Erebus carried Victorian explorers to the edge of Antarctica, then vanished with the Franklin expedition in the Arctic. Michael Palin follows the ship's whole life, from its launch to the discovery of its wreck in 2014. A lively, humane portrait of a ship and the people aboard.

books.title: Sea of Tranquility
books.author: Emily St. John Mandel
books.tagline: An anomaly that echoes across five centuries.
books.blurb: An exiled Englishman in a Canadian forest in 1912, a novelist on a book tour centuries later, and a man raised in a colony on the moon all brush against the same strange moment. Following its echoes, time itself becomes the puzzle. Elegant, tender speculative fiction.

books.title: Babel
books.author: R. F. Kuang
books.tagline: Translation is magic, and magic is power.
books.blurb: Orphaned in Canton and brought to Oxford, Robin Swift trains at the Royal Institute of Translation, where silver bars inscribed with words power the British Empire. The more he learns, the more he sees what the magic is for. A dark academic fantasy about language and colonialism.

books.title: Mexican Gothic
books.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
books.tagline: A mouldering mansion, a family with secrets.
books.blurb: In 1950s Mexico, glamorous Noemí Taboada receives a frantic letter from her newly married cousin and travels to the remote house of High Place to check on her. Its English owners are cold, the house is rotting, and something is growing in the walls. A deliciously creepy gothic horror.

books.title: The Thursday Murder Club
books.author: Richard Osman
books.tagline: Four pensioners, one murder, plenty of cake.
books.blurb: In a peaceful retirement village in Kent, four friends meet weekly to puzzle over unsolved cases. When a real killing happens on their doorstep, they find they are rather good at this. A cosy, witty mystery with a surprising amount of heart.

books.title: Magpie Murders
books.author: Anthony Horowitz
books.tagline: A murder mystery inside a murder mystery.
books.blurb: An editor settles in with the new manuscript from her bestselling crime writer, a classic village whodunit set in the 1950s. But the final chapters are missing, and the author may have hidden a real crime in the pages. An ingenious double puzzle for golden-age fans.

books.title: The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle
books.author: Stuart Turton
books.tagline: Same day, new body, until he solves it.
books.blurb: At a masquerade party at a crumbling country house, Evelyn Hardcastle will be killed at eleven. Aiden Bishop must relive the day in the body of a different guest each time until he finds the murderer. Agatha Christie meets a time loop, with a twist in every chapter.

books.title: The Only Good Indians
books.author: Stephen Graham Jones
books.tagline: One elk hunt. Ten years later, payback.
books.blurb: Four young Blackfeet men break the rules on a hunt and kill something they should not have. A decade on, something is following them. A horror novel about guilt, identity and tradition, frightening and deeply moving at once.

books.title: Bunny
books.author: Mona Awad
books.tagline: An MFA cohort that's sweet, and sinister.
books.blurb: Samantha is a scholarship student at an elite New England writing programme, repelled by the clique of rich girls who call each other Bunny. Then they invite her to their secret workshop. A wild, satirical horror story about loneliness and making things up.

books.title: The Searcher
books.author: Tana French
books.tagline: A retired detective. A village that doesn't talk.
books.blurb: Cal Hooper leaves the Chicago police for a quiet life in a run-down cottage in the West of Ireland. Then a local kid asks him to find a missing brother. French's slow-burning mystery is as much about a landscape and its silences as about the crime.

books.title: Razorblade Tears
books.author: S. A. Cosby
books.tagline: Two ex-con fathers, out for justice.
books.blurb: Ike, a Black man, and Buddy Lee, a white man, have little in common but prison records and the sons they lost, a married couple murdered in Richmond. Together they set out to find the killers. A ferocious Southern noir about grief, prejudice and redemption.

books.title: My Sister, the Serial Killer
books.author: Oyinkan Braithwaite
books.tagline: Bleach, a dead boyfriend, and family loyalty.
books.blurb: In Lagos, Korede is the reliable nurse who always knows how to clean up blood. Her beautiful younger sister Ayoola keeps killing her boyfriends, and when Ayoola sets her sights on the doctor Korede loves, something must give. A darkly comic, razor-sharp debut.

books.title: His Bloody Project
books.author: Graeme Macrae Burnet
books.tagline: 1869. A Highland crofter. Three bodies.
books.blurb: In a remote Scottish hamlet, seventeen-year-old Roderick Macrae confesses to a brutal triple killing. Presented as found documents, his memoir and the trial records leave the reader to weigh the truth. A literary thriller that was shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

books.title: Ninth House
books.author: Leigh Bardugo
books.tagline: Yale's secret societies practise real magic.
books.blurb: Alex Stern, a dropout who sees ghosts, is offered a full ride to Yale on one condition: she must watch over the university's secret societies, whose rituals are dangerously real. When a girl dies, she suspects the societies know why. Dark academia with a hard edge.

books.title: Things We Lost in the Fire
books.author: Mariana Enriquez
books.tagline: Buenos Aires stories, unsettling and political.
books.blurb: In these stories, the ordinary streets of Argentina open onto the uncanny: a dirty boy who vanishes, a haunted hotel, women who set themselves alight. Enriquez blends horror with the country's memories of violence. Dark, vivid and impossible to shake.

books.title: How to Do Nothing
books.author: Jenny Odell
books.tagline: Reclaim your attention from the attention economy.
books.blurb: Jenny Odell, an artist in Oakland, argues that doing nothing is not laziness but a form of resistance to a culture that monetises every waking moment. Drawing on birdwatching, art and philosophy, she suggests ways to pay attention to the places and people around us.

books.title: Four Thousand Weeks
books.author: Oliver Burkeman
books.tagline: Time management for actual mortals.
books.blurb: The average human life lasts about four thousand weeks, and no productivity system will make it longer. Oliver Burkeman argues that accepting our limits is the start of using time well. Wise, funny and liberating, it is a self-help book that takes philosophy seriously.

books.title: Trick Mirror
books.author: Jia Tolentino
books.tagline: Nine essays on self-delusion online and off.
books.blurb: Jia Tolentino examines the forces that shape how we see ourselves: the internet, scams, weddings, athleisure and reality television. Personal and analytical at once, these essays probe the cultural contradictions we all live with. A defining voice of her generation.

books.title: The Argonauts
books.author: Maggie Nelson
books.tagline: Love, family and theory, entwined.
books.blurb: Maggie Nelson writes about falling in love with the artist Harry Dodge, her pregnancy, and the family they build. She weaves memoir with critical theory, testing ideas about gender, queerness and care against lived life. A genre-defying book of intellectual daring.

books.title: Being Mortal
books.author: Atul Gawande
books.tagline: What matters most, in the end.
books.blurb: A surgeon confronts how modern medicine handles ageing and dying, and how often it fails the people it treats. Gawande tells the stories of patients and of his own father. A humane, clarifying book about how to live well to the very end.

books.title: At the Existentialist Café
books.author: Sarah Bakewell
books.tagline: Freedom, being, and apricot cocktails.
books.blurb: In 1933, three friends in a Paris bar discuss a new philosophy over cocktails, and existentialism is born. Bakewell tells the story of Sartre, de Beauvoir, Heidegger, Camus and their circle, their ideas and their quarrels. An irresistible group portrait of a philosophical movement.

books.title: The Scout Mindset
books.author: Julia Galef
books.tagline: Seeing what's there, not what you want.
books.blurb: Julia Galef contrasts two mental stances: the soldier, who defends beliefs, and the scout, who wants to see the territory clearly. She explains why the scout mindset is rarer than we think and how to cultivate it. Practical, upbeat and full of good examples.

books.title: The Precipice
books.author: Toby Ord
books.tagline: Humanity's long future, and how to protect it.
books.blurb: An Oxford philosopher surveys the risks that could end our story: from asteroids and supervolcanoes to engineered pandemics and unaligned AI. Toby Ord estimates the odds and argues for safeguarding the vast future we might have. Sobering but ultimately hopeful.

books.title: The Book of Delights
books.author: Ross Gay
books.tagline: A year of small essays on joy.
books.blurb: For one year, the poet Ross Gay set out to write a short essay each day about something delightful. The results range from fig trees and high-fives to grief and racism. A warm, generous collection about paying attention to what sustains us.

books.title: The Anthropocene Reviewed
books.author: John Green
books.tagline: Our planet, reviewed on a five-star scale.
books.blurb: John Green reviews facets of the human-centred world, from Canada geese and air conditioning to the internet and the QWERTY keyboard. Each essay winds into reflection on wonder, illness and hope. Funny, personal and surprisingly profound.

books.title: The Tyranny of Merit
books.author: Michael J. Sandel
books.tagline: What's become of the common good?
books.blurb: Political philosopher Michael Sandel asks why winners in a meritocracy feel they deserve their success, and what that does to everyone else. He traces how this belief fuels resentment and polarisation. A provocative argument for the dignity of work.

books.title: Noise
books.author: Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony & Cass R. Sunstein
books.tagline: The hidden error in human judgement.
books.blurb: Two doctors given the same case, or two judges given the same crime, often reach very different conclusions. Kahneman, Sibony and Sunstein call this variability noise and show how much it costs. A practical guide to making better decisions.

books.title: The Gene
books.author: Siddhartha Mukherjee
books.tagline: The story of heredity, intimate and vast.
books.blurb: Siddhartha Mukherjee traces the gene from Mendel's peas and Darwin's finches to genome editing, interleaving the science with his own family's history of mental illness. A sweeping, humane history of one of the most powerful ideas in science.

books.title: Entangled Life
books.author: Merlin Sheldrake
books.tagline: Fungi made the world. Still running it.
books.blurb: Fungi are everywhere, in soil, air and our own bodies, yet we barely know them. Merlin Sheldrake introduces mycelial networks that link forests, yeasts that shaped civilisation, and moulds that solve puzzles. A mind-expanding tour of a hidden kingdom.

books.title: Underland
books.author: Robert Macfarlane
books.tagline: A journey into the world beneath our feet.
books.blurb: Robert Macfarlane descends into caves, catacombs, mines and glacier shafts, and to a nuclear waste vault built to last a hundred thousand years. Along the way he considers deep time and what we leave to the future. Nature writing at its most ambitious.

books.title: The Sixth Extinction
books.author: Elizabeth Kolbert
books.tagline: Watching an extinction, as it happens.
books.blurb: Elizabeth Kolbert travels from the Andes to the Great Barrier Reef to report on species disappearing in our lifetimes. Through frogs, bats and rhinos, she argues that humans are driving a mass extinction as dramatic as any in Earth's history.

books.title: An Immense World
books.author: Ed Yong
books.tagline: Every animal lives inside a different reality.
books.blurb: Ed Yong explores how animals perceive the world: the electric sense of fish, the ultraviolet vision of birds, the magnetic sense of turtles. Each creature lives in its own sensory bubble. A joyful book that makes the familiar feel strange.

books.title: The Hidden Life of Trees
books.author: Peter Wohlleben
books.tagline: Forests talk, share, and remember.
books.blurb: A German forester describes how trees communicate through their roots and fungal networks, care for their young and warn each other of danger. Peter Wohlleben's walk in the woods changes how you see every forest. Gentle, curious and full of wonder.

books.title: Lab Girl
books.author: Hope Jahren
books.tagline: A scientist's life, rooted in plants.
books.blurb: Hope Jahren grew up in a cold Minnesota town and found her calling in the laboratory. She tells the story of her career, her friendship with her lab partner Bill, and the lives of plants and trees. A memoir of science as love and as work.

books.title: The Invention of Nature
books.author: Andrea Wulf
books.tagline: The explorer who taught us nature is connected.
books.blurb: Alexander von Humboldt climbed volcanoes, mapped rivers and saw nature as an interconnected web of life. Andrea Wulf reveals how his ideas inspired Darwin, Thoreau and modern environmentalism. A vivid biography of a forgotten giant.

books.title: The Vital Question
books.author: Nick Lane
books.tagline: Why life looks the way it does.
books.blurb: Biochemist Nick Lane argues that energy holds the key to the origin of life and the evolution of complex cells. From hydrothermal vents to sex and death, he builds a bold theory. A demanding, exhilarating read for anyone curious about life's beginnings.

books.title: H Is for Hawk
books.author: Helen Macdonald
books.tagline: Grief, a goshawk, and learning to live.
books.blurb: After her father's sudden death, Helen Macdonald takes on the training of a goshawk, among the most difficult of birds. As she retreats into the hawk's wild world, she also traces the troubled life of the writer T. H. White. A remarkable blend of memoir and nature writing.

books.title: Wilding
books.author: Isabella Tree
books.tagline: A farm handed back to nature.
books.blurb: When their intensive farm in Sussex was failing, Isabella Tree and her husband let it run wild. Longhorn cattle, pigs and ponies roamed free, and rare birds and butterflies returned. An inspiring account of rewilding in practice.

books.title: Invisible Women
books.author: Caroline Criado Perez
books.tagline: A world built for men, measured.
books.blurb: From car crash tests to medical trials and office temperatures, data on human beings has defaulted to men. Caroline Criado Perez shows how this gap shapes women's lives, health and safety. An eye-opening, rigorously argued book.

books.title: Citizen
books.author: Claudia Rankine
books.tagline: Everyday racism, in lyric fragments.
books.blurb: Through poems, prose and images, Claudia Rankine records the small, constant aggressions that accumulate in the life of a Black American, from tennis courts to the checkout line. A book that invents its own form to make the reader feel what it describes.

books.title: Night Sky with Exit Wounds
books.author: Ocean Vuong
books.tagline: Family, war and desire, in luminous lines.
books.blurb: Ocean Vuong's debut collection moves between the Vietnam War, his family's journey to America and a young man's coming of age. Tender and fierce, the poems find beauty in the hardest places. Winner of the T. S. Eliot Prize.

books.title: Postcolonial Love Poem
books.author: Natalie Diaz
books.tagline: Love poems as acts of resistance.
books.blurb: Natalie Diaz writes of desire, water, language and the bodies of Native people in America. Her poems are sensuous and urgent, insisting on the right to love and to live on the land. Winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry.

books.title: Deaf Republic
books.author: Ilya Kaminsky
books.tagline: A town falls silent, and resists.
books.blurb: When soldiers shoot a deaf boy during a protest in an occupied town, the people stop hearing, and communicate in sign. Ilya Kaminsky tells their story in a sequence of poems like a play. A haunting fable of resistance and tenderness.

books.title: Don't Call Us Dead
books.author: Danez Smith
books.tagline: An afterlife where Black boys are safe.
books.blurb: Danez Smith opens with an imagined heaven for Black men killed by police, then turns to desire, HIV and the nation's violence. The poems blaze with anger, grief and joy. Winner of the Forward Prize for Best Collection.

books.title: Wade in the Water
books.author: Tracy K. Smith
books.tagline: America's voices, past and present.
books.blurb: Tracy K. Smith weaves letters from Black soldiers of the Civil War, the Declaration of Independence and voices from today into poems about history, faith and motherhood. Quiet, searching and politically powerful.

books.title: The Carrying
books.author: Ada Limón
books.tagline: What we carry, what carries us.
books.blurb: Ada Limón writes of horses, fertility, a failing body and the beauty of the world in hard times. Her poems are direct and tender, finding consolation in close attention. Winner of the National Book Critics Circle Award.

books.title: The Tradition
books.author: Jericho Brown
books.tagline: Beauty and threat, in the same breath.
books.blurb: Jericho Brown's poems look at the Black body, queer love and the ever-present threat of violence. He invents a new form, the duplex, to hold their contradictions. Winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry.

books.title: Hamilton: The Revolution
books.author: Lin-Manuel Miranda & Jeremy McCarter
books.tagline: The full libretto, plus the story.
books.blurb: The complete text of Lin-Manuel Miranda's hit musical, annotated by the composer himself, alongside an account of how the show came to be. A behind-the-scenes look at the making of a cultural phenomenon.

books.title: Sweat
books.author: Lynn Nottage
books.tagline: A factory town's friendships, coming apart.
books.blurb: In a Reading, Pennsylvania bar, workers from the local steel tubing plant drink, celebrate and argue. As layoffs loom, loyalties crack. Lynn Nottage's Pulitzer-winning play captures the human cost of deindustrialisation.

books.title: The Inheritance
books.author: Matthew Lopez
books.tagline: Gay New York, haunted by history.
books.blurb: Inspired by E. M. Forster's Howards End, Matthew Lopez's two-part play follows young gay men in contemporary New York and their relationship with the generation that lived through the AIDS crisis. An epic of love and legacy.

books.title: The Hill We Climb
books.author: Amanda Gorman
books.tagline: An inaugural poem for a wounded nation.
books.blurb: Amanda Gorman delivered this poem at the 2021 presidential inauguration, at twenty-two the youngest inaugural poet in American history. Its call for unity and hope resonated worldwide. A keepsake edition.

books.title: The Wild Robot
books.author: Peter Brown
books.tagline: A robot learns to live with nature.
books.blurb: After a shipwreck, a robot named Roz washes up on a remote island with no idea how she got there. To survive, she must learn from the animals, and slowly she becomes part of their world. A gentle, funny adventure about kindness and belonging.

books.title: The Girl Who Drank the Moon
books.author: Kelly Barnhill
books.tagline: A witch, a baby, accidental magic.
books.blurb: Every year the people of the Protectorate leave a baby in the forest for the witch. But Xan, the witch, is kind and carries the babies to new homes, until one year she accidentally feeds one moonlight and fills her with magic. A Newbery-winning fairy tale.

books.title: New Kid
books.author: Jerry Craft
books.tagline: New school, new rules, same Jordan.
books.blurb: Seventh-grader Jordan Banks loves drawing cartoons but is sent to a prestigious private school where he is one of the few kids of colour. Navigating two worlds, he finds his way with humour. The first graphic novel to win the Newbery Medal.

books.title: The Crossover
books.author: Kwame Alexander
books.tagline: Twin brothers, basketball, poetry in motion.
books.blurb: Josh and Jordan Bell are twin basketball stars, but their bond is tested on and off the court. Told in vivid verse that bounces like a ball, this is a story about family and growing up. Winner of the Newbery Medal.

books.title: Brown Girl Dreaming
books.author: Jacqueline Woodson
books.tagline: A childhood told in poems.
books.blurb: Jacqueline Woodson recalls growing up in the 1960s and 70s, between South Carolina and Brooklyn, in the shadow of Jim Crow and the civil rights movement. Each poem is a memory of becoming a writer. Winner of the National Book Award.

books.title: The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse
books.author: Charlie Mackesy
books.tagline: Four friends, and the courage to ask.
books.blurb: A boy, a mole, a fox and a horse wander through the countryside together, talking about kindness, fear and friendship. Charlie Mackesy's ink drawings and handwritten words have comforted readers of all ages.

books.title: The Last Cuentista
books.author: Donna Barba Higuera
books.tagline: The last storyteller, on the last ship.
books.blurb: When a comet destroys Earth, Petra Peña and her family flee on a spaceship. Centuries later she wakes to find that the ship's new rulers have erased humanity's memories, and only she remembers the stories her grandmother told. Winner of the Newbery Medal.

books.title: Nevermoor
books.author: Jessica Townsend
books.tagline: A cursed girl finds a magical city.
books.blurb: Morrigan Crow is cursed to die on her eleventh birthday, but at midnight she is whisked away to the magical city of Nevermoor. To stay, she must pass trials for a mysterious society. A whimsical adventure full of delights.

books.title: Pax
books.author: Sara Pennypacker
books.tagline: A boy and his fox, separated by war.
books.blurb: Peter rescued Pax when he was a kit, but when war comes and his father enlists, Peter is forced to abandon him. Both boy and fox set out on a journey to find each other. A moving story about loyalty.

books.title: The Explorer
books.author: Katherine Rundell
books.tagline: Stranded children survive the Amazon.
books.blurb: After a plane crash in the Amazon jungle, four children must work together to survive. When they discover a ruined city hidden in the forest, they find they are not quite alone. A thrilling adventure about courage and wonder that won the Costa Children's Book Award.

books.title: Front Desk
books.author: Kelly Yang
books.tagline: A motel, a family, a girl's courage.
books.blurb: Ten-year-old Mia Tang and her immigrant parents manage a motel in California for a ruthless owner. While her parents secretly hide immigrants, Mia runs the front desk. A heartfelt story about family and standing up for what's right.

books.title: When You Trap a Tiger
books.author: Tae Keller
books.tagline: Grandmother's stories come to life.
books.blurb: When Lily and her family move in with her sick grandmother, a magical tiger appears, promising to heal Halmoni in return for stolen stories. A moving tale of family, folklore and courage. Winner of the Newbery Medal.

books.title: The Dawn of Everything
books.author: David Graeber & David Wengrow
books.tagline: Human history was never one straight line.
books.blurb: An anthropologist and an archaeologist challenge the story that humans moved inevitably from small egalitarian bands to cities, kings and states. Drawing on new evidence, they show our ancestors experimented with many ways of living together. A bold rethink of the human past.

books.title: Between the World and Me
books.author: Ta-Nehisi Coates
books.tagline: A letter from father to son.
books.blurb: Written as a letter to his teenage son, Ta-Nehisi Coates reflects on what it means to inhabit a Black body in America. Drawing on history and his own life, he confronts the nation's past and present. A profound, essential book.

books.title: Educated
books.author: Tara Westover
books.tagline: A survivalist childhood, then the classroom.
books.blurb: Tara Westover grew up in the Idaho mountains with survivalist parents who distrusted schools and hospitals. She first set foot in a classroom at seventeen. Her memoir traces an extraordinary journey of self-invention.

books.title: Say Nothing
books.author: Patrick Radden Keefe
books.tagline: A disappearance, and the Troubles.
books.blurb: In 1972, Jean McConville, a widowed mother of ten, was taken from her Belfast home by masked intruders. Patrick Radden Keefe uses her case to explore Northern Ireland's conflict and its legacy. Gripping narrative history.

books.title: Evicted
books.author: Matthew Desmond
books.tagline: Housing, poverty and profit in America.
books.blurb: Matthew Desmond follows eight families in Milwaukee struggling to keep a roof over their heads, and the landlords who profit from them. He shows that eviction is a cause, not only a consequence, of poverty. Winner of the Pulitzer Prize.

books.title: Born a Crime
books.author: Trevor Noah
books.tagline: Growing up mixed-race under apartheid.
books.blurb: Trevor Noah was born to a Black mother and a white father at a time when their union was illegal in South Africa. His memoir is hilarious and harrowing, and a love letter to his fearless mother.

books.title: Caste
books.author: Isabel Wilkerson
books.tagline: The hidden hierarchy underneath American life.
books.blurb: Isabel Wilkerson argues that America has a caste system, a rigid hierarchy that has endured since slavery. She compares it to India and Nazi Germany and shows its human cost. A powerful and illuminating book.

books.title: Bad Blood
books.author: John Carreyrou
books.tagline: A Silicon Valley startup built on lies.
books.blurb: Theranos promised to revolutionise blood testing with a single drop, and its founder became a billionaire. John Carreyrou, the journalist who exposed the fraud, tells the full story. A page-turning account of hubris and deception.

books.title: The Five
books.author: Hallie Rubenhold
books.tagline: The forgotten lives of Jack the Ripper's victims.
books.blurb: Hallie Rubenhold tells the stories of the five women killed in Whitechapel in 1888, restoring their lives and challenging the myths that have reduced them to victims. A powerful work of social history.

books.title: Chernobyl
books.author: Serhii Plokhy
books.tagline: The nuclear disaster, and the Soviet state.
books.blurb: Serhii Plokhy tells the story of the 1986 Chernobyl disaster, from the night of the explosion to its political aftermath. He shows how the accident exposed the failings of the Soviet system.

books.title: Hidden Figures
books.author: Margot Lee Shetterly
books.tagline: The Black women who calculated the space race.
books.blurb: During the space race, a group of Black women mathematicians at NASA calculated the trajectories that sent astronauts into orbit. Margot Lee Shetterly brings their extraordinary story to light.

books.title: Know My Name
books.author: Chanel Miller
books.tagline: A survivor reclaims her story.
books.blurb: Known to the world as Emily Doe, Chanel Miller was sexually assaulted on the Stanford campus. In this memoir she reclaims her identity and tells her story in her own words. A powerful indictment of a system that fails survivors.
